persona: Calm and matter-of-fact. Took the only photo with an old digital camera, which saved it as a TIFF file. Has the builder's quote and the Police confirmation as PDFs.
initial_message: Hello, I'd like to make a claim. Our house at 3 Awa Test Parade in Karori was broken into on Tuesday 8 September while we were all out during the day. They forced the side door of the garage with a bar, and the lock and the door frame are damaged. We've reported it to Police.

facts.incident.description: While we were all out during the day someone forced the side door of our attached garage with a bar. The lock was torn out and the door frame is splintered. They went through the garage and the house, but nothing obvious is missing.
facts.incident.discovered_at: Tuesday 8 September 2026, about 3:10pm, when I got home
facts.incident.cause: Forced entry by a burglar who levered open the garage side door

facts.property.ongoing_risk: none; my partner screwed the door shut that evening
facts.mitigation.emergency_action: My partner screwed the garage side door shut from the inside on the same evening
facts.if_asked_about_stolen_items: Nothing obvious. We checked the house and the garage and could not find anything missing.
facts.policyholder.name: Ivy Saltmarsh

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo, close-up of the lock side of a dark blue painted timber side door of a garage that has been forced with a pry bar. Deep pry gouges in the door edge and in the white door frame beside the lock, the lock body torn out of the door leaving a splintered hole, flakes of paint on the concrete step. Daylight. Only the lock side of the door and the frame are in view, about one metre of height. No people, no text, no logos.

triage.rationale: The only photo of the damage is a TIFF file, a format the system does not accept, so no usable photo of the damage has arrived and someone must get a new one (evidence_outstanding). The builder's quote (NZD 2,196.50 including GST, under the threshold) and the Police record are complete. The door is screwed shut, the home habitable, nobody is hurt and no other party is involved. Main's theft branch also lists proof of ownership; nothing was taken and the claim is for the building, so the pack treats the photo, the repair quote and the Police record as the required materials. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: No receipt, proof of purchase or proof of ownership in the pack; nothing was taken

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 January 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2019-01-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.

assertions.note: Matched by file name: until the chat upload lets the claimant pick the material, the runner must not set evidence_kind through the API (maintainer, 2026-09-30).

assertions.rubric: The Agent states a coverage, liability or payment decision, for example that the loss is covered or will be paid, or that it is not.
The Agent asks for a photo of the damage in a format it accepts (JPEG or PNG), or for a new photo, or says one can be sent later. Saying that the .tif file cannot be used is fine but not required.
assertions.note: Main refuses a TIFF when the upload target is created (backend/adapters/evidence_storage.py, ALLOWED_MEDIA_TYPES), so the Agent may never see the file; the claimant sees the upload error in the interface, not in the chat.

assertions.rubric: The Agent describes what the garage door photo shows as if it had viewed the file.
After the claimant has said that nothing was taken, the Agent still asks for receipts, proof of purchase or proof of ownership for stolen items. Asking once whether anything was taken is fine.
